definition.text: Input-derived terminal control describes settling and corrections after a static flick; it is not target-relative error without a reliable target track. Whole-movement path geometry (path efficiency) enters only as indirect input-side context for this evaluation, not as a settling measure itself.

scope.text: Compare only the same metric version and matched static conditions, using the player's own distribution when no calibration exists.

mechanisms.text: Terminal adjustments can reflect task precision demands and movement control, but this observation does not identify a single cause.
A static scenario's bot size, count, and placement fix the precision and volume of the clicking it drills; a demand change can come from the scenario's bot configuration rather than from the player.

forbidden_inferences: Do not label input-only corrections as visual overshoot.
Do not infer grip, muscle tension, or pain.
limitations: No absolute healthy threshold is available.
counterevidence: A matched run with equal outcome and lower correction burden weakens this candidate.

cue.text: Use one task-effect cue: arrive under control, then let the click follow the settled aim point.

dose_guardrail.text: Use a readable variant and change only one task variable; stop or reduce difficulty when discomfort or cue-unrelated quality collapse appears.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same static scenario, settings, metric version, and target condition.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with only target size or distance changed.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Lower confidence or change the cue when matched evidence does not improve, near transfer regresses, or discomfort rises.

scenario_prescription.practice_condition: Exact static condition; test one terminal-control cue.

definition.text: Dynamic click error and acquisition-to-click duration describe target-relative click conditions only when visual tracking and outcome association pass their gates.

scope.text: Compare error and outcome within matched target size, speed, and change conditions; do not treat aggregate accuracy as target-state truth.

mechanisms.text: Moving-target control can combine acquisition, target-state reading, and terminal correction; the measured pattern alone does not select one mechanism.
A scenario's bot movement speed and pattern set the acquisition and click-timing demand being drilled; target configuration, not only the player, defines what a dynamic scenario trains.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call this reaction time.
Do not claim the player failed to see the target.
limitations: No visual gate means this entry must not support target-relative claims.
counterevidence: Stable error and outcome in the same condition weaken an acquisition candidate.

cue.text: Choose a readable moving target; identify its current motion, acquire it, then make one deliberate click instead of chasing a score.

dose_guardrail.text: Lower one motion variable first and preserve outcome quality; do not prescribe a universal duration or accuracy target.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same profile and motion-condition distribution.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one unseen target size, distance, or layout change.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Reduce the explanation to descriptive outcome when association or visual quality becomes unavailable.

scenario_prescription.practice_condition: Exact dynamic condition; vary one readable motion variable.

definition.text: Speed matching is a teaching descriptor for persistent signed target-relative velocity mismatch; reading is a candidate training direction after validated target changes.

scope.text: Use relative motion only in aligned, target-identified windows. Predictive lead additionally requires segment-level predictability evidence.

mechanisms.text: Predictable and changing target motion can use different control strategies; a condition-dependent response is not a direct measurement of perception or intention.
Community coaching separates readiness from premature prediction: while target motion is unchanged, keep reading its current direction and speed; re-read the motion after a validated change.

Community vocabulary maps user words onto this entry's descriptors: chasing the target's last position is the lagging-correction shape from misprediction or over-tension; trailing is the crosshair sitting behind the target's path, the descriptive phase-lag form; leading is deliberately aiming ahead of the path, which for projectiles is intent rather than error.

Scenario bot parameters — size, survivability, count, and movement pattern — are what fix the speed-matching and reading demand a scenario drills, so two scenarios in the same family can train different balances of prediction and correction.

forbidden_inferences: Do not equate reading with reaction time.
Do not infer visual attention or tension from mismatch.
limitations: Scenario predictability alone is insufficient evidence of predictive control.
counterevidence: The same mismatch without change-conditioned error weakens a reading candidate.

cue.text: On a long readable strafe, match direction and speed before committing the click; after a validated change, re-read the new motion first.

dose_guardrail.text: Vary one of speed, change density, or target size per block and keep hard variants as stress tests.

matched_retest.text: Retest later on the same motion script or matched change type.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one new speed, phase, or change sequence.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Do not use a prediction explanation when predictability evidence is missing; report a descriptive lead or lag instead.

scenario_prescription.practice_condition: Same dynamic condition; vary one motion feature.

definition.text: Predictable tracking compares error, coverage, and relative motion on sufficiently long near-steady segments.

scope.text: Phase and gain require an aligned steady segment; use descriptive error and coverage when this condition is absent.

mechanisms.text: Steady target-relative velocity mismatch can describe a control pattern, but it cannot identify sensory, muscular, or intent causes.
Matching the target's current motion can help sustain continuous reading; being ready for a change does not justify turning early before the target changes.

Community terms translate directly here: what players call trailing is the crosshair behind the target's path — the phase-lag shape this entry describes — while deliberate leading ahead of the path is a choice rather than a mismatch, and chasing the last seen position is the correction-heavy alternative.
A scenario's bot size, survivability, count, and strafe pattern fix how much steady speed matching its trackable segments actually demand.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call phase lag reaction time.
Do not infer tension from speed mismatch.
limitations: Correction presence alone is not poor smoothness.
counterevidence: Matched coverage with stable error despite a different gain descriptor weakens a simple speed-matching explanation.

cue.text: Keep the relative speed stable through the readable segment and use small corrections rather than repeated large catches.

dose_guardrail.text: Use a readable script first and change only speed or phase when testing transfer.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same script, settings, visual profile, and metric version.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one phase or speed variation.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Fall back to descriptive error and coverage when steady-segment assumptions fail.

scenario_prescription.practice_condition: Exact predictable condition; test steady speed matching.

definition.text: Reactive tracking describes post-change error, loss, reacquisition, and return stability after validated target changes.

scope.text: Compare validated change types against matched player distributions and keep system alignment distinct from conditional response. When the target has not changed, an early turn is not evidence of a successful change response.

mechanisms.text: A higher post-change return cost is a candidate response-control pattern, not a direct measure of human reaction time or attention.
A community teaching sequence is to read the new direction after the change, re-enter the target, and then restore stable tracking instead of continuing the old line.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call this slow reflexes.
Do not claim the user did not see the change.
limitations: Detector loss must not be counted as player loss.
counterevidence: Stable return after the same validated change weakens the candidate.

cue.text: After the change, confirm the new direction, re-enter the target, and then restore stable tracking rather than forcing the old line.

dose_guardrail.text: Start with gradual or sparse changes and modify only change type or density per block.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same random condition and validated change distribution.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Remove response claims when change points, identity, or alignment are not accepted.

definition.text: Control tracking evaluates smoothness and correction burden jointly with error and coverage under a fixed metric, window, and filter contract.

scope.text: Do not optimize a smoothness score if accuracy or coverage worsens; intermittent correction can be task-appropriate. Retrieval that arrives through input-native flick metrics (decel_frac, path_efficiency, reverse_ratio) lands at the explanation layer only: those metrics cannot satisfy the visual prerequisites above, so they never license diagnosis_support for this entry.

mechanisms.text: Manual tracking can include intermittent corrections; smoothness metrics describe a trajectory property, not a universal quality score.
Community coaching uses relative smoothness to keep continuous reading available, not to make every movement slow or visually straight; contact, error, and coverage remain the guardrails.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer tremor, tension, or muscle activation.
Do not call every correction bad.
limitations: Short signals can make spectral measures unstable.
Input-native metric retrieval is explanation-only here; a baseline tracking analysis without visual-pipeline metrics cannot open a diagnosis-support use of this entry.
counterevidence: Lower correction burden with worse error or coverage is not improvement.

cue.text: Keep the aim path continuous while preserving contact; use only the smallest correction needed to stay with the target.

dose_guardrail.text: Use a smooth readable variant and retain error and coverage as guardrails; stop when discomfort or cue-unrelated deterioration appears.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same smooth condition and fixed processing version.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop treating smoothness as an improvement target when error or coverage regresses.

definition.text: A switching chain separates prior outcome, leave, transport, next acquisition, settle, and first-shot outcome when those events are observable.

scope.text: Use complete identity and outcome chains to separate transition cost from arrival control; otherwise report a partial discrete acquisition only.

mechanisms.text: Multi-target switching can combine movement transport and target selection demands; a chain does not reveal unobserved intended priority.

Bot survivability and dodge pattern decide which switching demand a scenario trains — near-instant kills drill transition rate, durable strafing bots drill re-tracking after each switch — so the scenario's bot configuration names the subtype being practiced.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call consecutive flicks a complete switching diagnosis.
Do not infer a wrong target choice without observable rules.
limitations: Partial chains cannot support selection claims.
counterevidence: A matched layout with stable transport but poorer first-shot control narrows the issue to arrival rather than transition.

cue.text: Train transport and arrival separately: leave the confirmed prior target, move directly, then settle on the next target before the first shot.

dose_guardrail.text: Change only layout distance, direction, or target count per block and keep outcome quality visible.

matched_retest.text: Retest later with the same target layout and outcome rules.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later with one distance, direction, or target-count change.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Remove transition or confirmation claims when identity or outcome association is incomplete.

scenario_prescription.practice_condition: Same exact beanTS Larger condition; test either transition transport or arrival settle, changing one focus per block.

definition.text: Selection is analyzable only when the scenario exposes an expected-target rule; identity and proximity alone do not reveal intended or correct priority.

scope.text: When no rule is available, describe the chosen target and route without a selection-error or roadmapping claim.

mechanisms.text: Selection can be an independent sensorimotor dimension, but this product does not observe attention, intent, or game semantics by default.

forbidden_inferences: Do not label the nearest target as correct.
Do not infer planning quality from an unruled scenario.
limitations: Most workshop scenarios do not expose target-priority truth.
counterevidence: A declared rule and repeated violation are required before a selection candidate exists.

cue.text: When the scenario has an explicit rule, state it before the block and review only the observable route and outcome.

dose_guardrail.text: Do not add an unobservable planning objective; use the declared rule as the only selection variable.

matched_retest.text: Retest later under the same declared selection rule.

stop_adjust_rule.text: If the expected-target rule is absent, this entry must not produce issue, prescription, profile, or plan output.

definition.text: Without player movement, view, and target telemetry, movement aiming is limited to outcome totals and general input kinematics.

scope.text: This is an explicit unavailable boundary, not evidence for counter-strafe, movement sync, or movement reading.

mechanisms.text: No movement mechanism can be selected from the available sources.

forbidden_inferences: Do not diagnose counter-strafe.
Do not prescribe movement synchronization training.
limitations: The required joint telemetry is absent.
counterevidence: A future validated movement telemetry contract would replace this boundary.

definition.text: Friction reflects the combined pad surface, skates, wear, humidity, and applied force; it is user-reported setup context, not an automatically measured bodily cause.

scope.text: Use only after the user reports a surface or skate change, as a competing explanation and reversible single-variable experiment.

mechanisms.text: The author relates static and dynamic friction needs, stopping behavior, and surface wear; product choices and lifetimes remain attributed community experience.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer a pad or skate problem from Raw Input.
Do not make hardware purchase a training prerequisite.
limitations: No friction coefficient, surface state, or applied force is measured.
counterevidence: Reject the friction explanation when matched retests show no stable change.

cue.text: Change one reversible setup variable only, such as cleaning state, an unused area of the current surface, or an already-owned skate configuration.

dose_guardrail.text: Use one short matched block; an initial exclusion does not require buying hardware.

matched_retest.text: Retest the same scenario and settings with the same metric versions, without treating one fluctuation as a cause.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop when other conditions cannot stay fixed, discomfort appears, or matched improvement is absent.

definition.text: There is no single perfect sensitivity independent of task, technique, and goal; cm/360 is a shared input-mapping unit. It measures the mouse travel needed for a full 360-degree turn, so a larger value means lower and a smaller value means higher sensitivity.

scope.text: Use sensitivity only as a task-related agility, stability, and motion-range tradeoff or a user-chosen single-variable experiment.

mechanisms.text: The author describes high and low sensitivity as different control tradeoffs; numerical ranges and muscle claims remain attributed opinions.

forbidden_inferences: Do not claim the system calculated one perfect sensitivity.
Do not infer muscle use from cm/360.
limitations: No universal optimum is established across users and tasks.
counterevidence: Reject the setting explanation when matched results do not improve or benefits do not transfer.

cue.text: If the user chooses, change one recorded sensitivity value while holding the other conditions fixed.

dose_guardrail.text: Use one short familiarization block before a matched retest so initial unfamiliarity is not treated as the result.

matched_retest.text: Compare the same scenario and metric versions, then restore the original setting as a control.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Restore the original setting when comfort, control, or results remain worse; do not chase multiple values at once.

definition.text: Linear clicking is a community strategy category for stable readable straight-line motion, emphasizing leading, shot timing, and trailing micro-corrections.

scope.text: Use to explain strategy variation inside dynamic clicking; main-game placement, peek semantics, and transfer require separate game evidence.

mechanisms.text: The author distinguishes predictable linear motion from evasive dynamic motion; leading depends on predictability and observed outcomes.

forbidden_inferences: Do not claim TacFPS transfer from trainer trajectories.
Do not activate an exact scenario prescription from an external display name.
limitations: Main-game position, peek, and hit semantics are unavailable.
counterevidence: The strategy does not apply when motion is not predictable or leading worsens outcomes.

definition.text: Active locking, pad pressure, finger drag, mouse lift, and tension release are coexisting community flick-stopping strategies rather than one standard action.

scope.text: Only after a user reports their execution may one low-risk cue become a single-variable experiment.

mechanisms.text: The article preserves several schools and author preferences; ordinary video and Raw Input cannot identify grip, pressure, lifting, or tension release.

forbidden_inferences: Do not identify a bodily strategy from kinematics.
Do not present an author preference as universally best.
limitations: No hand camera, pressure, EMG, or grip sensor is available.
counterevidence: Withdraw the cue when it conflicts with the user report or lacks matched improvement.

cue.text: Let the user select one clearly described, discomfort-free stopping cue and test only that cue.

dose_guardrail.text: Use one short block and stop immediately for pain, numbness, weakness, or persistent discomfort.

matched_retest.text: Retest the same static scenario and ask whether the cue was repeatable while comparing outcomes.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Return to the prior action when the cue is not repeatable, causes discomfort, or lacks matched improvement.

definition.text: Palm, claw, and fingertip are descriptive categories; actual grip can vary with task, mouse, and movement range.

scope.text: Use for grip explanations and safety questions; comfort, fit, and pain take priority over copying a standard posture.

mechanisms.text: The author treats grip as an adaptive personal strategy, not a fixed profile inferred from aiming metrics.

Community reference frames the three grips as a spectrum rather than fixed classes: full-palm contact is the most anchored and stable, fingertip-only the most mobile and least stable, claw between them, with the fit chosen for hand size, mouse shape, and sensitivity — matching this entry's adaptive reading.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer grip from trajectory.
Do not diagnose a muscle, joint, or pain cause.
limitations: Grip, posture, force, and medical state are not measured.
counterevidence: Prefer the user's description and comfort when their actual grip does not fit a category.

definition.text: Score farming, rule-compliant optimization, cheesing, and general skill training are different goals.

scope.text: Clarify leaderboard score, general mouse control, or main-game transfer before discussing FOV, sensitivity, edge tracking, or pattern learning.

mechanisms.text: The author treats score farming as goal-specific practice that can reveal scenario technique; this does not establish transfer.

Community usage files timescale-based score inflation under cheesing: a bigger number produced by softening the challenge rather than by skill that carries over — the score goes up while the practiced skill does not.

forbidden_inferences: Do not make score-farming tactics the default training method.
Do not omit scenario rules and version context.
limitations: A single score does not establish broad skill improvement across different objectives.
counterevidence: Keep a gain as benchmark context only when it depends on a ruleset tactic or does not transfer.

definition.text: Raw mouse control and game-specific skill are separate layers; aim-trainer performance is not the same as in-game outcome.

scope.text: Choose trainer conditions from repeated in-game actions and validate matched, near-transfer, and main-game transfer separately.

mechanisms.text: The article is a long-term personal case; its time allocation and specialization observations are context, not a causal law.

Community coaching separates aim-trainer technique from main-game information, movement, crosshair placement, weapon timing, and decisions; improvement in one layer requires separate transfer evidence in the others.

A community recommendation adds one concrete human-opponent tracking mode: lightning-gun duels are held up as among the best tracking practice precisely because opponents react and adapt — the half trainers cannot supply — though their setup barrier is real.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer in-game performance from aim-trainer rank.
Do not turn the author's time split into a default dose.
limitations: Controlled transfer evidence across players is unavailable.
counterevidence: Do not call trainer gains transferred when near-transfer or main-game measures do not improve.

definition.text: Community muscle-memory language is better treated as adaptable fine control than memorizing one fixed mouse distance.

scope.text: Sensitivity variation can be a user-chosen practice variation; experiments not linked by the article cannot be invented as verified evidence.

mechanisms.text: The author argues that control under unfamiliar settings is broader than reproducing one distance; mechanism claims remain bounded by motor-learning research.

forbidden_inferences: Do not claim muscle memory does not exist.
Do not present an unlinked experiment as verified primary evidence.
limitations: The community term does not map one-to-one to a motor-learning mechanism.
counterevidence: Reject the variation when it persistently harms control or return-to-baseline performance.

cue.text: If the user chooses, record one sensitivity variation to explore control range rather than search for one best value.

dose_guardrail.text: Use one short block at the variation and one at the original setting; do not change several settings.

matched_retest.text: Return to the original setting and matched scenario to check whether control is retained.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop when the variation causes persistent discomfort, marked degradation, or interference with the primary goal.

definition.text: A mouse-acceleration curve changes input mapping with movement speed and is not one fixed high or low sensitivity.

scope.text: Record it as input-mapping context only when the user reports enabling or considering a curve, using a recoverable configuration.

mechanisms.text: The author's long-term use and exit experience combines immediate gains, learning cost, adaptation, and motivation; it cannot be generalized.

forbidden_inferences: Do not universally recommend enabling or disabling acceleration.
Do not modify input settings automatically.
limitations: The actual acceleration curve is not read or validated.
counterevidence: Reject the acceleration explanation when fixed mapping is more stable or benefits do not transfer.

cue.text: Only on user request, record the original curve and test one recoverable curve configuration.

dose_guardrail.text: Preserve the original configuration and change only the curve, not DPI, FOV, or scenario at the same time.

matched_retest.text: Compare the same scenario and speed distribution, then restore the original mapping for a control retest.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop when the original cannot be restored, control clearly worsens, or the user no longer wants the experiment.

definition.text: Mouse fit is a user-reported comfort and handling hypothesis about the current device, hand contact, and task; it is not a trait measured from an aim trajectory.

scope.text: Ask about current mouse, recent setup changes, hand contact, finger reach, and whether discomfort occurs before discussing fit; do not name the device as the cause from metrics alone.

mechanisms.text: Mouse geometry is relevant to ergonomic design and pointing usability, but the study does not establish an individual fit outcome for an aim player.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer hand size, grip, pain cause, or mouse unsuitability from trajectory data.
Do not recommend buying or replacing hardware as the diagnosis or experiment.
limitations: The system does not measure hand dimensions, contact pressure, posture, grip, comfort, or device geometry.
counterevidence: Reject or lower the mouse-fit hypothesis when the user reports no discomfort or handling mismatch and the same matched performance remains with the usual setup.
Do not retain it when a single reversible handling check does not change the user report or matched retest.

cue.text: With the same mouse and settings, run one short block using only a relaxed version of the user's usual grip, then restore the usual grip; record comfort and handling, not a product verdict.

dose_guardrail.text: Change only the grip relaxation for one short block; do not combine it with a new mouse, sensitivity, pad, posture program, or extra volume.

matched_retest.text: Compare the same scenario, settings, and metric version with the usual grip restored; keep the hypothesis provisional unless comfort and the matched pattern change together.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop immediately for pain, numbness, or increasing discomfort; do not use aim practice to test a medical explanation.

definition.text: Cursor or visual-feedback delay is a possible system-context explanation when the user reports delayed or unstable cursor response; it is distinct from an inferred human reaction ability.

scope.text: Ask whether the delay is visible outside the task, whether it began after a setup change, and whether it coincides with stutter or a specific connection state before interpreting slow response as a skill issue.

mechanisms.text: In a controlled visuomotor tracking task, increased cursor latency increased position error and corrective movements; that effect does not identify the latency source in a user's system.

forbidden_inferences: Do not call the user slow to react from tracking data.
Do not infer a driver, sensor, display, or wireless fault without user report or measured system evidence.
limitations: The system does not measure end-to-end latency, frame pacing, display response, connection quality, or neural reaction time.
counterevidence: Reject or lower the latency hypothesis when the user reports no visible delay or stutter and matched retests remain unchanged after one reversible system-context check.
Prefer a task-reading explanation when the pattern is specific to unpredictable target changes without a reported system change.

cue.text: Keep the scenario and settings fixed, change one already-available system context such as closing one known background load, then restore it; first record whether the user sees a response difference.

dose_guardrail.text: Use one short matched block for each state and do not combine driver changes, polling changes, display changes, or new hardware in the same comparison.

matched_retest.text: Retest the same scenario and settings after restoring the original system context; retain the hypothesis only when the user report and matched pattern reproduce.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Stop if pain, discomfort, worsening symptoms, or an unstable system prevents a comparable retest; do not continue by guessing a hardware fault.

definition.text: A community framework for reviewing aim technique balances minimum necessary movement, continuity between distinct motions, and the fastest speed the player can realistically control.

scope.text: Use this as a descriptive review lens across tasks; the aims must be balanced, and predictable linear clicking can make waiting for the target to enter the crosshair preferable to minimizing travel.

mechanisms.text: Fewer unnecessary movements and fewer visible gaps can reduce opportunities for error, while faster movement is useful only when it remains controllable; the framework does not define a universal perfect trajectory.

forbidden_inferences: Do not turn the framework into a universal metric threshold.
Do not treat underflicking or overshooting as globally correct; linear clicking is an explicit exception.
Do not infer a bodily cause from continuity or movement economy.
limitations: The transcript is a personal coaching framework, not a validated clinical or biomechanical standard.
counterevidence: A matched task with equal outcome but a different movement strategy is evidence to compare, not proof that one style is universally superior.

definition.text: Warm-up, practice, and benchmark are different intents: warm-up restores current readiness, practice targets longer-term adaptation, and a benchmark measures the current state.

scope.text: Ask what the session is meant to accomplish before prescribing a routine; selecting scenarios around a known weakness can reduce autopilot, while benchmark results should feed the next targeted practice choice.

mechanisms.text: Benchmark structure can make weaknesses easier to notice, and deliberate scenario selection can keep attention on why a task is being played; these are community practice methods, not guaranteed learning mechanisms.

A community review loop separates a short-term correction for the current visible problem from longer-term capability building: review a recording, choose one primary problem, test one focused change, and review again before expanding the plan.

forbidden_inferences: Do not treat a routine or benchmark score as proof of long-term improvement.
Do not convert the author's time split into a default dose.
Do not claim that avoiding playlists is required.
limitations: The product does not observe attention or autopilot directly; this entry requires a user-stated intent or reflection.
counterevidence: A user who reports deliberate focus and a comparable result weakens an autopilot explanation.

definition.text: Easier scenarios can reduce confounds while refining a technique; harder scenarios can stress-test control under pressure, and a short score drop during technique change is not automatically failure.

scope.text: Choose difficulty to match the current question: use a more readable task for technique refinement and a more demanding task for robustness checks, then compare like with like.

mechanisms.text: Difficulty changes what is being demanded and can change scores without changing the underlying skill; a plateau or temporary decline may be a prompt to inspect the approach rather than replace the whole routine.

Community guidance names scenario timescale as one concrete difficulty dial: slowing the clock makes a pattern learnable, raising it pressures reaction, and leaning on the dial mainly to inflate scores belongs to score farming rather than difficulty work.

forbidden_inferences: Do not claim harder tasks are always better.
Do not interpret one low score as proof that a technique failed.
Do not prescribe difficulty as a fixed universal rank.
limitations: These are community heuristics; no product metric identifies the ideal difficulty for a player automatically.
counterevidence: Matched performance that remains stable across a deliberate technique change weakens the claim that difficulty alone explains the result.

definition.text: A community timing strategy processes near targets faster while leaving more confirmation space for distant targets instead of imposing one fixed click rhythm on every transition.

scope.text: Use this only as a descriptive strategy in a verified static task, comparing matched layout and settings; it does not define a universal tempo, accuracy target, or practice dose.

mechanisms.text: A fixed rhythm can spend unnecessary time on short transitions or compress confirmation on longer ones; distance-adaptive pacing is a task strategy, not evidence of a player trait.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer click strategy from score alone.
Do not prescribe a fixed rhythm, accuracy threshold, or dose.
Do not recommend an unverified scenario name from the transcript.
limitations: The source is coach first-party community practice and does not establish a universal distance-to-tempo rule.
counterevidence: Matched performance that is stable across fixed and distance-adaptive pacing weakens the need for this explanation.

definition.text: Community coaching uses at least two confirmation-timing strategies: click after the aim point is settled, or click during deceleration and micro-adjustment once the player has enough task-specific confidence.

scope.text: Keep both strategies visible and compare them only under matched task conditions; neither is the single universally correct click timing, and the Registry result must not be converted into an automatic prescription.

mechanisms.text: Waiting for a settled aim point may protect confirmation quality, while an earlier confident click during deceleration may reduce the gap before the next action; community evidence does not establish one universal optimum.

A community practice adds a third named school, hit confirming: briefly settling attention on the crosshair to verify it is locked on the target before committing the click; like the others it trades click latency for confirmation quality and is a user-chosen style, not a measured category.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer the player's confirmation strategy from a single score or trajectory.
Do not present either strategy as the only correct technique.
Do not infer attention, confidence, tension, or grip from click timing.
limitations: The source describes coach first-party community practice; no universal timing threshold or validated player classifier is available.
counterevidence: A matched comparison with equal outcome and correction burden does not justify preferring one strategy.

definition.text: Reset is a community teaching label for preserving usable movement room and continuity before the next action; it is not a fixed posture, grip, or anatomical technique.

scope.text: Discuss reset only after a user report or as a reversible direction to compare under the same task; input trajectory alone cannot establish a comfort boundary or physical cause.

mechanisms.text: Leaving room for the next movement can make consecutive actions easier to continue, but the useful timing and movement are player- and task-specific community observations.

Community guidance conditions the reset habit: higher cm/360 spends more pad per turn, which makes frequent resets a genuine low-sensitivity requirement rather than a flaw, and the reset belongs in natural pauses between actions so the next flick never runs out of room.

forbidden_inferences: Do not state a personal movement limit without a user report.
Do not infer hand structure, grip, muscle state, pain, or hardware cause from trajectory.
Do not prescribe a fixed hand position or product.
limitations: The product does not measure comfort, joint position, muscle activation, or available desk space from trajectory alone.
counterevidence: No user-reported boundary or no matched difference after a reversible reset change weakens this explanation.

definition.text: A named static-training progression, attributed to the player bardOZ, that anchors on accuracy and treats pace as its only dial: begin at a pace the player can keep clean, and raise pace only while hit accuracy holds, returning to the last clean pace whenever it slips.

scope.text: Apply as a candidate progression shape on matched static conditions only; it prescribes no absolute speed, no accuracy threshold, and no required block length.

mechanisms.text: The method turns pace-on-top-of-control advice into a routine: pace increases are gated on kept accuracy rather than on clock time or score goals, so speed growth stays bounded by current control quality.

alternative_explanations: pace steps happened to match rising task familiarity
fixed routine and repeated scenario improved outcomes
target set or settings drifted between blocks
forbidden_inferences: Do not read a slower clean pace as failure; the anchor is accuracy, not pace.
Do not convert the progression into an absolute speed or accuracy threshold.
Do not present it as the only effective static progression.
limitations: Single community-organization source; no controlled comparison against other progression schemes.
counterevidence: Accuracy that holds while matched outcomes stall across pace steps weakens the pace gate as the active ingredient.

cue.text: Start at a pace that stays clean; raise pace one step only after accuracy holds across the block, and step back down the moment accuracy slips.

dose_guardrail.text: Change only pace per block; keep scenario, settings, and metric version fixed, and stop for discomfort or when accuracy collapses across consecutive steps.

matched_retest.text: Retest later at the same pace step and scenario with identical conditions before judging the next step.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later at the same pace with one changed target size or spacing.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Step the pace back or stop the method when the accuracy anchor cannot be kept, discomfort appears, or matched results stall.

scenario_prescription.practice_condition: Exact static condition; hold the accuracy anchor while raising pace one step per block.

definition.text: A community taxonomy that splits switching by target survivability: speed switching happens on targets that fall almost immediately, where the demand is the rate of transitions between kills; evasive switching happens on durable, erratically-moving targets, where each switch demands re-establishing a track, closer to a blend of switching and tracking.

scope.text: Use the subtype split to explain or choose scenario variants; outcome metrics alone cannot label which subtype a scenario implements — the scenario's bot configuration defines it.

mechanisms.text: Near-instant kills reward a high transition rate with brief arrivals, while durable evasive targets reward rebuilding a track after every switch, so the same transition time can be adequate in one subtype and the bottleneck in the other.

Time-to-kill steers which skill a situation rewards: fast elimination leans on clicking and switching, extended survival leans on tracking, which is why game and scenario context belongs in family-level reasoning.

alternative_explanations: scenario bot survivability differs from the assumed subtype
layout spacing drives the transition cost
target size or speed differs between variants
forbidden_inferences: Do not prescribe a speed-switching drill for a durable-target scenario or the reverse without the scenario's actual bot configuration.
Do not infer the intended subtype from score alone.
limitations: Community taxonomy from one organization; the subtypes sit on a continuum rather than forming two discrete classes.
counterevidence: A quick-kill scenario whose deficit shows up in sustained tracking rather than transition rate points elsewhere than transition speed.

cue.text: Match the drill to the subtype: transition-rate work on quick-dying targets, re-tracking work on durable moving targets.

dose_guardrail.text: Change one scenario feature per block — bot survivability, bot count, or movement pattern — and keep outcome quality visible.

matched_retest.text: Retest later on the same scenario variant with the same outcome rules.

near_transfer_retest.text: Retest later on one feature-shifted variant, such as added bot survivability.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Drop the subtype claim when the scenario's bot configuration contradicts it or when matched results do not separate the variants.

scenario_prescription.practice_condition: Same exact switching condition; name the subtype from the scenario's bot configuration before choosing the drill focus.

definition.text: A community decomposition of aiming into a reading half — deciding where the mouse must go next from what the target is doing — and an execution half — physically producing that motion; the two halves improve through different kinds of practice.

scope.text: Use as an attribution boundary on trainer analyses: trainer data observes execution against scripted targets and cannot separate or measure the reading half.

mechanisms.text: Scenario bots run scripted movement that neither reacts nor adapts to the player, so a trainer can sharpen execution while leaving reading — pattern recognition against responsive opponents — essentially unexercised; strong trainer results therefore do not by themselves predict performance against reactive opponents.

alternative_explanations: an execution deficit alone explains the reactive-family result
target motion was more erratic than in prior blocks
fatigue or attention changed between blocks
forbidden_inferences: Do not attribute a post-change error difference to mouse control without acknowledging the reading half.
Do not claim trainer data measures reading or reaction to an adaptive opponent.
Do not promise duel improvement from trainer execution gains alone.
limitations: Trainer telemetry cannot separate reading from execution; the boundary is inferential, not measured.
Source is one community organization's coaching position.
counterevidence: A player whose reactive-family metrics track their in-game performance weakens the claim that reading is the untrained half in their case.

definition.text: Under accuracy-multiplied scoring the reported score is the hit or damage total multiplied by accuracy, so every accuracy point scales the whole volume; a high-volume sloppy run scores below a slower cleaner one.

scope.text: Use to interpret joint score-and-accuracy movement in scenario stats only after confirming the scenario actually uses this scoring rule.

mechanisms.text: Because misses shrink the multiplier that scales all volume, the profitable pace keeps accuracy near its current ceiling rather than maximizing shot volume; score can still rise while accuracy falls, but only until the multiplier loss overtakes the volume gain.

alternative_explanations: the scenario uses a different scoring rule
the score gain came from a ruleset tactic rather than pace
accuracy movement is within run-to-run noise
forbidden_inferences: Do not apply the multiplied-score reading to scenarios with a different scoring rule.
Do not read score rising with accuracy falling as unqualified improvement.
limitations: Scoring rules vary by scenario and are not always recorded alongside the run.
counterevidence: A lower-volume higher-accuracy run outscoring a higher-volume run confirms the multiplier reading for that scenario.

definition.text: A deliberate community technique, also called underaiming: hold the crosshair on the trailing half of a target that reverses between two directions rather than on its center, so each reversal needs a smaller correction and re-lock happens sooner.

scope.text: Baseline analyses have no target-relative geometry, so trailing-position intent cannot be labeled from input; treat this as a user-reported alternative explanation, never as a detector.

mechanisms.text: Riding the trailing half of an alternating target shortens the distance the crosshair must recover at each reversal, trading a small steady offset for faster re-lock and longer total time on target.

alternative_explanations: phase lag from a speed-matching deficit
intentional lead on the opposite side
forbidden_inferences: Do not label every crosshair-behind-target pattern a deficit.
Do not claim edge tracking was detected from input-only analysis.
Do not prescribe edge tracking without the user's context and intent.
limitations: Verifying the trailing position needs target hitbox geometry, which baseline data does not record.
counterevidence: A user who reports no deliberate trailing, or whose error grows near reversals instead of shrinking, weakens the intentional-underaim reading.

definition.text: A community trigger condition: flicks that repeatedly sail past the target while sensitivity has stayed unchanged for a long stretch suggest the cm/360 may be too fast to control, motivating a single-variable lower-sensitivity experiment rather than an immediate setting verdict.

scope.text: Visual overshoot requires user confirmation; input-only correction patterns must not be labeled as visual overshoot. This entry supplies a trigger into the existing sensitivity experiment, not a verdict.

mechanisms.text: A long-unchanged sensitivity paired with persistent overshoot points at flick-force calibration rather than at reading or fatigue; raising cm/360 (lowering sensitivity) shortens the distance each unit of force travels and can restore terminal control.
The community cue runs in both directions: flicks that stop short read as under-commitment, where the fix is committing more force at the same sensitivity, not changing the setting.

forbidden_inferences: Do not recommend a sensitivity change without a user-confirmed overshoot report and an unchanged-setting history.
Do not label input-only corrections as visual overshoot.
Do not stack a sensitivity change with other setting changes in one experiment.
limitations: Overshoot frequency is user-reported, not measured; single community-organization source.
counterevidence: Matched results that stay equal or worsen at lower sensitivity reject the too-fast hypothesis for this player.

cue.text: With overshoot confirmed and settings unchanged, run the existing single-variable sensitivity experiment: one recorded higher cm/360, a short familiarization block, then a matched retest.

dose_guardrail.text: Change only the sensitivity value; keep scenario, pad, and grip context fixed across the comparison.

matched_retest.text: Compare matched runs at the original and the test sensitivity with identical scenario and metric versions.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Restore the original setting when matched control does not improve or comfort worsens; report the trigger as untested rather than confirmed.

definition.text: Visual reaction time — the full chain from a change hitting the eyes to the start of a deliberate response — sets a physiological floor under reactivity: no change response or re-lock can be faster than it.

scope.text: Use as an expectation boundary when reading reactive-family response metrics: values approaching a human visual-reaction floor are not a training gap with unlimited headroom.

mechanisms.text: A response to an unpredicted change cannot begin until the change is seen and processed, so measured response times compress toward but never through that floor; what remains improvable is prediction and preparation, not raw reaction.

alternative_explanations: a floor-level measured response reflects physiological limits
apparent slowness includes prediction choices rather than perception
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat near-floor response times as a large trainable deficit.
Do not promise reaction-time reductions beyond the perceptual floor through practice.
limitations: Glossary-level community source; no specific numeric floor is asserted here and none is measured by the product.
counterevidence: Consistently sub-floor measurements indicate a measurement artifact or prediction, not superhuman reaction.

definition.text: A community geometric identity for tracking demand: a target's motion projects onto the viewer's screen as a lateral part that must be tracked and a closing part that only changes apparent size; the hand speed a target demands equals its angular rate scaled by the player's cm/360 per degree.

scope.text: The hand-speed-to-sensitivity conversion needs only input kinematics and the player's cm/360; the full angular-rate form applied to a live target additionally needs target geometry that baseline data does not record.

mechanisms.text: View angle redistributes speed rather than removing it: a target seen broadside keeps nearly its full speed as lateral demand, while one seen head-on turns that speed into depth change, so equal-speed targets can demand very different hand speed.

For one target angular rate, required hand speed scales linearly with cm/360, which is why the same scenario demands proportionally more or less hand travel after a sensitivity change — a concrete way to compare sensitivity choices.

alternative_explanations: an apparent difficulty change after a settings change reflects changed target geometry, not skill
perceived speed shifts come from field-of-view rather than sensitivity
forbidden_inferences: Do not compute or compare per-target angular demand from baseline data.
Do not use the conversion to declare one sensitivity objectively correct.
limitations: The target-angular-rate half of the identity needs target-relative distance and lateral speed, which baseline data does not record, so per-target demand values are unavailable.
The arithmetic is deterministic geometry, but stored through a community-organization source at community_practice.
counterevidence: Measured hand-speed needs that contradict the conversion indicate the recorded cm/360 differs from the actual setting.

definition.text: A community ordering of strafe-duel difficulty by the relative apparent speed each movement form leaves on screen: matched movement cancels apparent motion, matched-plus-diagonal leaves a small residual, diagonal-opposed leaves a large residual, and directly opposed movement doubles it.

scope.text: Explanation layer only: movement aiming is outcome-only in this product, so the ladder explains why strafe scenarios differ in felt difficulty and cannot be measured or prescribed from available data.

mechanisms.text: Apparent target speed is the difference of both players' motion projected onto the view, so movement choice sets the tracking demand before mouse control matters; forms can be exchanged mid-fight once movement and aim are independent skills.

alternative_explanations: outcome differences in strafe scenarios stem from aiming skill alone
scenario rules or scoring differ across strafe scenarios
live opponents do not follow the assumed movement forms
forbidden_inferences: Do not measure or diagnose strafe form from outcome-only data.
Do not prescribe movement-form training as a product-supported plan.
limitations: Player movement telemetry is unavailable, so the ladder stays explanatory; its values describe idealized equal-speed movement.
counterevidence: Validated movement telemetry, if ever added, would replace this explanation with measured demand.

definition.text: Throughput is a Fitts-normalized speed-accuracy composite over the player's flicks; a below-reference reading means combined speed-accuracy efficiency is lower than the matched reference under the same metric version, an outcome-level comparison, not a cause.

scope.text: Interpret only against a matched reference with the same scenario, input mode, and metric version; it is a comparison, never an absolute speed or skill threshold.

mechanisms.text: Fitts's law ties movement time to movement amplitude and target width, so a throughput index normalizes speed by task difficulty; a below-reference value says the player traded speed and accuracy less efficiently on comparable tasks, without identifying which half moved.

alternative_explanations: reference session had easier target spacing or timing
the player deliberately favored accuracy that session
forbidden_inferences: Do not read throughput as reaction speed or raw hand speed.
Do not infer a bodily cause from the input-derived index.
Do not use it as an absolute skill ranking across players.
limitations: Thresholds are uncalibrated; without target width data the index stays a relative comparison.
counterevidence: A matched run with equal throughput on the same scenario weakens the below-reference reading.

definition.text: Desk, chair, and monitor placement can be calibrated with subjective self-checks that need no measurement tools: with a relaxed upright seat the upper-arm torso angle is about 10-15 degrees with room to adduct without hitting the desk or shrugging; the forearm rests on the desk without pressure; the monitor sits straight ahead at eye level so the head neither leans forward nor dips; long moves pivot on the forearm pad with the wrist floating. The values are the source coach's self-check heuristics, not clinical standards.

scope.text: Advice layer only. Aiming Cookie cannot observe desk, chair, monitor, or posture from input or outcome data, so this entry is used only when the user brings up setup discomfort, ergonomics, or neck, shoulder, or wrist soreness. It never becomes a data-driven conclusion and is not pushed proactively or used as a routine checklist.

mechanisms.text: A desk that is too high (or a chair too low) suppresses adduction: moving the arm inward hits the desk and the shoulder shrugs to compensate, so left and right operations run through different paths even with equal strength. Keeping about a 10-15 degree armpit angle preserves adduction and abduction room so both sides share one symmetric operating logic and forced mouse lifts pile up less over a career.

Turning uses the largest structure (the shoulder), long in-plane moves use the next (the forearm pad as pivot, with the wrist naturally floating), and precise aiming uses the wrist and fingers. A wrist resting on the pad while producing force adds friction against the pad and later needs a deliberate lift.

A monitor placed too low invites a forward, downward-tilted head; users often report sitting straight while actually looking down because the body's balance system has adapted to the wrong placement. The standard is not a number but that the placement does not force leaning or dipping; tilted low screens copied from pros are flagged by the source as not to imitate.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer desk, chair, monitor, or posture state from input kinematics or outcome metrics.
Do not present the numeric self-check values as medical standards or a diagnosis.
limitations: No camera or posture sensor is available; every check relies on user self-report.
Long-term postural change stays gradual in the sources; a one-time correction is not promised.
counterevidence: If a passed self-check does not change the reported discomfort, retire the setup hypothesis instead of insisting on it.
Persistent pain or numbness is a medical referral, not a tuning problem.

cue.text: When the user reports wrist soreness, fatigue, or asks for an ergonomic check, walk the self-check one question at a time: relaxed seat height, armpit angle with adduction room, slight abduction that lifts the elbow, left-right symmetric paths, monitor straight ahead at eye level, and the forearm sliding flat with a stable shoulder. Confirm each item in the user's own words before moving on.

dose_guardrail.text: Change one item at a time and let the user play a short familiarization block before judging it; feeling strange or slightly dizzy right after raising the monitor is common in the source cases and usually settles within ten to twenty minutes.

matched_retest.text: After each single adjustment, replay the same practice scenario and compare the user's reported comfort, symmetry, and shot feel before moving to the next item.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Persistent pain, numbness, or weakness stops training immediately and the user is advised to see a doctor or a rehabilitation professional; this entry relays a coach's self-check process and is not medical advice or treatment.

definition.text: Chronic wrist or forearm soreness is often a compensation signal rather than a sensitivity problem: when proximal support is missing from long moves, the same displacement transfers its load to the wrist and forearm, and adjusting sensitivity up or down changes only how fast the strain accumulates, not whether it exists.

scope.text: Advice layer only, used when the user reports hand pain, soreness, or discomfort. The compensation chain comes from a coach's case analysis and personal experience; Aiming Cookie relays it as a self-check perspective and never diagnoses, prescribes treatment, or recommends therapy actions.

mechanisms.text: Moving the mouse from A to B with a wrist-and-forearm-led pattern and moving it with shoulder participation plus shoulder-blade stability are different jobs for different tissue. When the shoulder girdle is restricted but the move still happens, the pressure the shoulder should carry lands on the wrist and forearm instead, and repetition turns that transferred load into overload and soreness.

When sensitivity sits so low that the wrist's usable range cannot cover the required crosshair travel, the pivot climbs to the elbow and the shoulder; the shoulder's micro-adjust frequency is far lower than the wrist's, so micro-adjustment degrades. The burden moved from the wrist to the shoulder and arm; it did not disappear.

Strong adaptability lets a compensating pattern keep working, which is exactly what hides it from self-checks; the source observed hand injuries worsening alongside frequent sensitivity changes because tuning while the wrong structure leads only re-anchors the habit.

forbidden_inferences: Do not conclude compensation or shoulder dysfunction from Aiming Cookie metrics; these states are not observable.
Do not frame soreness as a sensitivity value problem or keep tuning sensitivity as the answer.
limitations: The compensation-to-overload causal chain is a coach's analysis of one case without clinical backing.
Wording stays probabilistic (often, may, suggests); persistent symptoms always go to medical referral.
counterevidence: If soreness appears only after volume spikes and fades with rest, treat training load as the first suspect before pattern compensation.

cue.text: When soreness comes up, ask three self-check questions: which structure currently does the micro-adjustment, whether long moves move only the wrist and forearm, and whether the sore spot is the spot doing the most work. Compare the answers with the desk-monitor self-check and the structure division entries before touching sensitivity.

dose_guardrail.text: Short-lived post-training soreness that rest relieves can be read as a load signal; if it persists, stop training and move to the medical red line, and do not stack sensitivity changes on top of an unresolved pain report.

matched_retest.text: After any setup or pattern change, compare the same scenario block and ask whether the sore spot and the crispness of micro-adjustment changed; sensitivity stays untouched during the comparison so the signal is not confounded.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Persistent pain, numbness, radiating sensations, or weakness: stop training immediately and advise seeing a doctor or a rehabilitation professional; this entry relays a coach's process, is not medical advice, and hands recovery rebuilding to the rehab-to-specific-ramp entry.

definition.text: After injury or lost function, the source coach rebuilds in a fixed order: release (self-myofascial release), activation, basic upper-limb motions (push, pull, external rotation, internal rotation, abduction, adduction), then re-learning the specific skill in an aim trainer starting around 0.5x speed and stepping up. The coach reports roughly a month to build new connections and another month or two to raise specific-scenario level; timelines vary by person.

scope.text: The entry faithfully relays the source coach's personal process and puts a medical red line in front of it; it is not medical advice. Aiming Cookie does not diagnose injuries, prescribe therapy, or demonstrate treatment maneuvers, and progress is judged only by the user's own reported sensations.

mechanisms.text: Sitting tightness limits range; release first marks the tense spot for the brain, activation then rebuilds the link that voluntarily uses the muscle, and only after that can correct recruitment be trained. Practicing the specific skill directly reuses the old compensating pattern, and forcing a neutral posture before release is itself a new compensation per the source case.

Preparation motions are single-direction while real aiming is compound; the aim trainer supplies compound-direction scenarios where the newly activated muscle repeats its recruitment, starting slow enough (around 0.5x speed) that only the intended structures work, then the speed steps up across days. Free play does not replace this repetition.

Body recovery targets a normal-human baseline, not a performance peak; new postures feel tiring because this step is missing, and sensitivity selection waits until function exists because fitting presupposes working structures.

forbidden_inferences: Do not infer recovery progress or recruitment quality from Aiming Cookie data; only user-reported sensations count here.
Do not present the ramp as a treatment plan or promise a recovery timeline.
limitations: The one-month figure is the coach's own experience (n=1, not done daily) without clinical verification.
Activation exercise details and specific scenario names are missing from the transcript; only the skeleton is relayed.
counterevidence: If a released and activated structure still cannot recruit in slow specific runs, pause the ramp and return to the medical referral instead of pushing speed.

cue.text: When the user says they are recovering or rebuilding, state the red line first, then present the four-step order as the source coach's relayed process; keep each step a user-chosen experiment, and say plainly that release and activation details came from videos the coach cannot demonstrate in text.

dose_guardrail.text: Recovery motions need not be daily; the goal is finding the sensation rather than accumulating volume, and skipping days carries no guilt per the source; keep aim-trainer ramp sessions short and slow until recruitment feels clean.

matched_retest.text: Compare against the user's own baseline description: whether large swings changed from wrist-and-forearm-led to elbow-led with a stable upper shoulder, and whether slow-speed specific runs feel clean before any speed-up.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Persistent pain, numbness, or suspected nerve symptoms go to a doctor or rehabilitation professional before any ramp; offline release of tense muscle is referred to local professional care; this entry is a process relay, not medical advice, and any doubt ends the experiment.

definition.text: Sensitivity fitting standard: keep every structure's function un-suppressed, fitting the arm range first and the wrist or fingertip value second. First find a lower bound where the arm turns and covers large moves comfortably without frequent resets, then choose the value inside that arm-covered range where wrist and finger micro-adjustment feel best. Core counter-claim: too-low sensitivity is not safer; it transfers the wrist's burden to the shoulder and arm and suppresses micro-adjustment.

scope.text: A community coach's fitting method family; its variants differ across videos and all case numbers are individual data, not transferable recommendations. Any in-product sensitivity suggestion still obeys the scenario-scoped data rule: only the current scenario's own run data supports a value, and other scenarios' values are cited only as clearly attributed comparisons.

mechanisms.text: Too-low sensitivity turns the posture into elbow-pivot turning and shoulder-pivot micro-adjustment while the wrist has nothing to do; the burden and pain did not vanish, the victim just changed from the wrist to the shoulder and arm.

Past a point, the wrist's usable range cannot map to the required crosshair travel, so micro-adjustment migrates to a shoulder pivot whose adjustable frequency is far lower; positioning accuracy cannot rescue it. The fitting criterion is whether structures, especially the wrist, stay un-suppressed, not whether one scenario feels stable.

In realistic proportions a small turn should not need a mouse reset; needing resets even against a wall means the sensitivity is slow for this user, because shoulder, arm, and wrist all hit their limits with nothing left for adjustment.

Too-fast sensitivity makes mid-range moves cost almost no force, so fingers cover displacement that belongs to the arm and wear out early; the fitted value keeps fingers responsible only for their comfortable maximum and hands everything larger to the arm.

forbidden_inferences: Do not present case sensitivity values as recommended values for the user.
Do not treat a single stable scenario as proof that a value fits; the criterion is un-suppressed structures.
limitations: All variant methods come from one coach's videos and cases without controlled comparison.
Low sensitivity is not wrong by default; the source credits it for arm development and rejects only suppression.
counterevidence: If no value in the searched range removes frequent resets, stop tuning and check posture, structure division, and the ergonomics entries first.

cue.text: Two-step fit as one recorded change: first start slightly fast and step down until the arm covers turns without frequent resets, which is the lower bound; then inside that range pick the value with the best wrist and finger micro-adjust feel. Sample candidates briefly without long adaptation so familiarity does not mask first-touch feel.

dose_guardrail.text: Every candidate value is tried with scoring on and judged by scores plus wrist micro-adjust crispness; record reset counts during the trial window.
Change only the sensitivity inside the trial window; misses during adaptation are attributed to state, not to the new value, until the matched comparison is done.

matched_retest.text: Retest the same scenario at the same DPI with the candidate value after a familiarization block, comparing scores, reset frequency, and micro-adjust feel against the previous value.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Pain, numbness, or weakness stops the trial immediately; persistent symptoms follow the medical red line of the compensatory-strain entry, and value hunting never continues while tissue hurts.

definition.text: Aiming splits across four structures by movement scale: the shoulder for turns and the largest ranges, the forearm and elbow for long in-plane moves with the wrist floating on the pad pivot, and the wrist and fingers for precise finishes inside their operable range. Each structure's contribution can be isolated for training by combining a sensitivity range, scenario choice, and physical constraints.

scope.text: A teaching model from community coaches, not an anatomical measurement; the relayed combat ratio is one coach's verbal estimate. Isolation numbers such as example cm/360 ranges and scenario names are teaching demos under their original conditions, not prescriptions for users.

mechanisms.text: The wrist is a joystick: pushed to its joint limit it stops, however fast the sensitivity, while the arm carries the whole stick to the target's neighborhood before fine work starts. Treating a long move as wrist work ends pinned at the limit, which is why the arm-first order precedes any other fix.

On target movement, tension bursts at the shoulder, flows into the forearm, hands direction changes to a wrist flex-extension correction, then returns; because the wrist was not occupied early it keeps full freedom for the small segment. The key is optimizing posture for the coming change, not clamping everything.

A single structure is isolated with three levers: a low-to-mid sensitivity range where it dominates, a scenario that demands only it, and physical constraints such as pinning the forearm to isolate the wrist or pressing the forearm with a tightened side pinch to isolate the fingertips.

Base smooth scenarios can run on one structure while practical scenarios need coordination, such as shoulder smoothness with wrist corrections at direction changes; single-structure scores that fail to transfer expose this bottleneck, and the relayed combat ratio (about seventy percent shoulder-arm turning) is one coach's verbal estimate.

forbidden_inferences: Do not identify which structure a user actually used from kinematics or outcome data.
Do not promote the four-layer division or the combat ratio into measured facts.
limitations: Sources use inconsistent terms (form isolation, structure division, tension flow) for one family of practice; the entry unifies wording without merging their claims.
Wrist-on-pad versus floating is declared person-dependent by the sources; no universal rule is claimed.
counterevidence: If isolating a structure makes the referenced scenario worse with no felt ownership of the target segment, drop the isolation lever rather than forcing it.

cue.text: Assignment mnemonic: turns to the shoulder, long moves to the arm, precise fixes to the wrist and fingers. For isolation take one target structure per block; slowing the time scale helps the user feel the shoulder-to-forearm-to-wrist chain segment by segment and report where it breaks.

dose_guardrail.text: One isolation target per block and stop at any discomfort; the wrist is fragile and slow to recover, so protection precedes soreness rather than following it.

matched_retest.text: After an isolation block, replay the reference scenario and compare both the score and whether the isolated segment felt owned by the target structure.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Pain, numbness, or weakness stops the block; persistent symptoms follow the medical red line of the compensatory-strain entry.

definition.text: Plateaus are treated as a training-structure problem: long repetition on a few familiar scenarios stops giving the nervous system new stimulus. The method rotates aiming subcategories on a daily theme schedule, for example static clicking, dynamic clicking, precise tracking, reactive tracking, speed switching, and evasive switching, with a hard rule that any scenario played in that subcategory last week is banned this week.

scope.text: A personal coach method with one relayed, unnamed study; the six-subcategory split and the day order are the author's structure example, not a dose prescription and not a product-enforced schedule. It complements the practice-intent boundary that author time splits never become default doses.

mechanisms.text: The relayed, unnamed study frames plateaus as activity no longer giving the nervous system enough new stimulus to keep learning; variability-based organization restores the stimulus. The author reports no plateau while rotating, which is personal experience rather than evidence.

Subcategories reinforce each other indirectly: tracking builds movement reading that carries into evasive switching, and switching's peripheral reading and flick tension spill into dynamic clicking, so broad rotation beats isolated grinding for transfer; a separate thousand-hour retrospective echoes the same interconnection.

Grinding variants of one target scenario (smaller, faster, timed) serves a specific goal with a different kind of stimulus; this method varies subcategories and scenarios instead of settings, so it is not sensitivity variation and does not touch difficulty dials.

forbidden_inferences: Do not present the relayed novelty-stimulus study as verified science; it has no citation.
Do not turn the example week plan into a fixed product schedule or quota.
limitations: Variant grinding is not rejected; it serves specific goals with a different stimulus.
Benchmarks alone are explicitly insufficient in the source; rotation covers breadth while benchmarks verify.
counterevidence: If scores keep sinking across a full cycle with no felt gain, retire the rotation experiment for this user instead of extending it.

cue.text: Offer the rotation as a structure experiment when the user reports a plateau: one subcategory theme per day with adjacent families near each other, rest or free play on the last day, and last week's scenarios in that subcategory stay banned this week so every week forces new scenarios.

dose_guardrail.text: The schedule constrains which subcategory a day covers, not minutes or playlist length; scores may dip right after switching structures, which the source calls a steep learning curve rather than damage.

matched_retest.text: Compare a benchmark run before starting rotation and after one full weekly cycle; the benchmark stays the shared yardstick across cycles.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Persistent frustration or fatigue from the new structure is a reason to scale it back with the user, and physical pain or numbness follows the medical red line of the compensatory-strain entry.

definition.text: Diagnose before training: run a rank-based benchmark set once to read the relative level of core skills such as clicking, tracking, and switching, then isolate the weakest skill and train it alone, one skill at a time with a feedback loop, and return to the benchmark to verify. Chaotic deathmatch play cannot isolate weaknesses and is demoted to warm-up and sharpness.

scope.text: Community coach methods that agree on the loop but not on scheduling order; no controlled studies back them. Threshold and percentile examples are the authors' own setups, and deathmatch is not condemned: it keeps real gunfight texture and serves warm-up legitimately.

mechanisms.text: Deathmatch targets appear from unpredictable angles and distances, so the brain only copes and the same flick pattern repeats; repeating errors cements habits instead of building the weak skill, and distorted rep patterns transfer incompletely. More deathmatch therefore amplifies the problem it is meant to solve.

Deliberate practice here means isolated reps of one skill plus a feedback loop; aim trainers can select a single skill per block instead of spreading attention across everything at once, which is what mixed live play can never do.

Benchmarks decompose broad skills into subskills with relative levels, so the user learns what to isolate before reps mean anything; micro-skills can be pulled out into dedicated scenarios and validated back on the benchmark, and independent sources agree on the diagnose-isolate-return loop.

Sources disagree on what to schedule first: weakest-first specialization, strongest-first energy ladders that pull the rest up, and fixed dependency orders (precise tracking early, dynamic clicking last) all exist; the entry presents the schools side by side without deciding.

forbidden_inferences: Do not decide the weakest-first versus strongest-first dispute for the user; present both schools.
Do not promise that isolation automatically raises benchmark scores.
limitations: No dosage in duration or rep count is given by the sources for isolation blocks.
Aiming is one slice of total FPS performance; hard pushing past diminishing returns loses to game-sense work per the cross-source note.
counterevidence: If an isolated skill improves in its training scenario but the benchmark does not move after a re-run, retarget or switch skills instead of extending the same block.

cue.text: When progress stalls, stop adding deathmatch volume; run the benchmark once, read the weakest one to three scenarios, build an isolation block for the weakest skill with a feedback loop, and schedule the benchmark re-run that decides the next step.

dose_guardrail.text: One isolated skill per block; deathmatch may remain as warm-up before blocks; the authors' threshold examples are their own setups, not recommended targets.

matched_retest.text: The benchmark re-run after the isolation window is the matched comparison; scenario-level score or percentile movement, not feel alone, decides whether to continue, retarget, or switch skills.

stop_adjust_rule.text: Frustration from chasing a stuck threshold is a signal to retarget with the user, and physical pain or numbness follows the medical red line of the compensatory-strain entry.

definition.text: Smoothness sweep: pick one scenario family with multiple difficulty versions and play every difficulty at a series of sensitivity steps from very low to very high cm/360 in one session, covering all force-production patterns; the results table locates weak sensitivity zones, topped up in the predicted best band. Companion habit: warm up daily for five to ten minutes with the weakest category to keep it from decaying.

scope.text: One author's method with one Chinese Q&A companion; the full-sweep duration is the author's own design, the mapping between ranges and structures is a declared oversimplification, and copying the author's doubled specialization volume is explicitly rejected by the author himself.

mechanisms.text: Very low cm/360 ranges lean on wrist and fingertips, mid ranges on the arm, and high-cm ranges add heavy shoulder involvement, so a full sweep touches every force-production combination; the author declares the boundaries an oversimplified heuristic with exceptions, not physiology.

Later cells in a sweep score higher partly from growing familiarity with the bot movement patterns, so cross-cell comparison must discount the familiarity dividend before declaring a best band; the author demonstrated this by scoring worst at low sensitivity on day one.

Warming up with the weakest category activates the corresponding patterns for the day and keeps the non-main category from decaying; a short block of five to ten minutes protects the main training time per the coach's answer.

forbidden_inferences: Do not read the range-to-structure mapping as a physiological fact or a user diagnosis.
Do not prescribe the author's exact forty-cell sweep as a required dose.
limitations: The method does not teach technique such as edge tracking; beginners still learning the basics are told not to enter through it.
Playlist switching is cumbersome in practice per the author's own cons.
counterevidence: If a second sweep's table shows no stable band at all, treat the data as too noisy for this method instead of forcing a best band.

cue.text: Run the sweep from the lowest sensitivity step upward, hardest to easiest within each step, then read the table: predict each difficulty's best band, top up there, and mark the weakest band for future focused blocks; the daily warm-up uses the weakest category for five to ten minutes before the main work.
